items.title: Deep Dive: Is Iraqi Kurdistan headed towards two parallel administrations?
items.summary: Iraqi Kurdistan's revived regional legislature has raised the specter of its two ruling parties going their separate ways again, two decades after merging rival administrations. After the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) pushed the Kurdistan Parliament back into session on Nov. 4, Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) leader Bafel Talabani announced the next day, in a fiery video message, that his side was quitting the Kurdistan region’s government and did not recognize its…

ai.sum: Iraqi Kurdistan's revived parliament raised fears that the KDP and PUK may split into two parallel administrations.

items.title: Oil exports begin through Kirkuk–Ceyhan pipeline
items.summary: Iraq’s Ministry of Oil announced that crude oil exports have begun through the old Iraq–Turkey pipeline connecting the Kirkuk oil fields to the Port of Ceyhan in Turkey.
